finish_summary: Explored three RTL formulations of the 32-bit popcount: (1) the original ripple-chain-of-adds reference (baseline, 264.67 um^2, WNS 7.01636 ns, score 69.89893), (2) an explicit balanced pairwise-adder tree using generate blocks with minimal per-level bit widths, and (3) a SWAR/bit-trick (Hamming-weight) implementation using masks, shifts and a constant multiply-like shift-add reduction. Synthesis with Yosys/ABC evidently already normalizes the arithmetic into a near-optimal netlist regardless of RTL structure: the balanced-tree version (submission 1) produced an essentially identical gate count/area (264.67 um^2, 242 cells) with a marginally better WNS (7.01662 ns), yielding the best verified score of 69.90153. The SWAR bit-trick version, in contrast, synthesized to far more logic (675.64 um^2, 551 cells) due to the extra masking/shifting network and multiply-style final reduction, giving a substantially worse score (67.02036) despite being functionally correct (after fixing an initial indexing bug that failed the equivalence/simulation check). Given the two functionally-different RTL structures converged to essentially the same optimized result and the alternate algorithm was strictly worse, further restructuring is unlikely to yield significant gains under this synthesis flow. The best verified result is the balanced-tree implementation from submission 1, with score 69.90153 (area 264.67 um^2, WNS 7.01662 ns), which is selected as the final answer.
